description: How Bitcoin & Ethereum soared while Dogecoin and Shiba Inu detonated and imploded — a semi-annual market-cap race from 2015 to 2026 (2026 = estimate).
youtube_description:
00:00 — Intro: The Meme Coin Massacre
00:24 — What we’re racing: semi-annual market caps (2015 H1 → 2026 H1 est)
01:10 — Bitcoin’s climb: from single-digit billions to >$1T
02:05 — Ethereum’s surge and EIP milestones that mattered
03:08 — Dogecoin mania: the May 2021 pump that hit ~$80B
04:02 — Shiba Inu: token launch to top-20 market cap in 2021
05:00 — The crashback: 2022 deleveraging and regulatory shocks
06:10 — 2023–2025 recovery patterns and 2026 projection (est)
07:00 — TL;DR: winners, losers, and what the race teaches investors
07:40 — Sources & method
08:10 — Outro + call to action

Full story: This visualization tracks semi-annual market capitalizations (billions USD) for Bitcoin, Ethereum, Dogecoin and Shiba Inu from 2015 H1 through a 2026 H1 estimate. The dataset highlights two tectonic events: the 2017 crypto boom and the 2020–2021 meme-coin surge that pushed DOGE to ~ $80B market cap (May 2021) and SHIB into the top 20 with ~ $13B peak (late 2021), followed by the 2022 crash that erased hundreds of billions across crypto.

Why this matters: Bitcoin and Ethereum established long-term value growth (Bitcoin crossing $1T+ market cap in late 2021; Ethereum nearing $500B in the same period), while meme coins demonstrated extraordinary short-term volatility — explosive spikes and brutal drawdowns. The chart race style makes that contrast dramatic: one set of lines (BTC/ETH) climbs into the hundreds of billions and beyond, while DOGE/SHIB explode briefly then collapse and partially recover.

Sources: CoinMarketCap, CoinGecko, Messari, Glassnode charts and exchange-reported market caps (semi-annual snapshots). Specific reference points cited in-video.

If you want the spreadsheet or raw JSON used to create the race, comment below and I’ll drop a link.

Like, subscribe, hit the bell and share this video if you want more chart-race breakdowns of markets, memes and tech.

instagram_caption:
🚀 From pocket change to trillion-dollar headlines: the wild semi-annual race of BTC, ETH, DOGE and SHIB (2015 H1 → 2026 H1 est).

This is the story of two worlds colliding. On one side: Bitcoin and Ethereum — the slow, steady titans that climbed from single-digit billions (Bitcoin at ~$3.5B in 2015 H1) to the mind-bending peaks of 2021 (Bitcoin topping ~$1.1T market cap and Ethereum near ~$500B in 2021 H2). Their lines on the chart race keep rising, then correct, then climb again — turning crypto into a macro asset with real scale.

On the other side: the meme rockets. Dogecoin went from cents-and-memes to a peak market cap of roughly $80B in May 2021 — a single retail frenzy that lit up social media and trading apps. Shiba Inu, born in 2020, briefly crashed onto the top-20 list with roughly $13B at its late-2021 high. But the drama didn’t last: the 2022 crash blew away hundreds of billions across the sector. DOGE fell from ~$80B to tens of billions, SHIB collapsed toward single-digit billions and smaller.

What makes the race cinematic is contrast. Bitcoin and Ethereum turned two major bull cycles (2017 and 2020–21) into sustained market caps measured in the hundreds of billions; meme coins turned narratives, celebrity tweets and retail FOMO into massive, but fleeting, market-cap explosions. After 2022’s deleveraging, the survivors recalibrated: Bitcoin and Ethereum regained footing through 2023–2025; DOGE and SHIB settled into new, much-lower baselines — but still with the power to spike.

If you could freeze one moment from this race — the peak, the crash, or the recovery — what would you choose and why? Drop the year and the coin (e.g., “2021 DOGE”) in the comments — best picks get pinned.
